newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU sees lower beet sugar output in 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: EU sees lower beet sugar output in 1997/98.

text.p: European Union beet sugar output is expected to be about 650,000 tonnes lower in 1997/98 (July/June), compared with the 16.5 million tonnes produced this season, a European Commission official said on Thursday.

A preliminary estimate presented to the EU sugar management committee on Wednesday showed that although the sugar beet area was one percent higher than the 2.02 million hectares sown in 1996/97, the average yield was expected to fall to 7.78 tonnes per hectare, from 8.18 tonnes this season.
Lower yields reflect dry weather conditions in northern Europe earlier this year.

The official said "A" quota sugar production was expected to be about 60,000 tonnes higher, mainly due to increases in Portugal and Greece. "B" sugar out was also likely to be slightly higher. In Italy there was some confusion between growers' and industry estimates.
The production decline was expected to be entirely in "C" sugar. But the "C" sugar carry-forward into 1998/99 was tentatively put at one million tonnes, against 970,000 tonnes in 1997/98.
"The tendency towards a lower harvest means that there will be less available for the world market," the official said.
The estimate will be examined by the sugar committee on July 2. It will then be discussed with the sugar industry and processors on July 7 before an official estimate is issued on July 9.
EU 1997/98 (July/June) white sugar export tenders are expected to be opened on August 6, Commission officials said.

They added that the final 1996/97 tender will be held on July 30. The EU has for the last two seasons launched new export tenders in August, one month later than usual, reflecting a slower flow of exports.
The EU on Wednesday set the 1997/98 (July/June) most-favoured-nation (MFN) raw cane sugar import quota at 85,463 tonnes, Commission officials said.
The 12-months quota succeeds an 18 months quota and corresponds to 82,000 tonnes of white sugar.
It is shared between Cuba (69 percent), Brazil (28 percent) and other countries (3.0 percent) which benefit from a reduced tariff of 98 ecus a tonne.
The quota compensates Finland's traditional suppliers under the former General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) for trade losses after it joined the EU in 1995 and raised tariffs.
The EU agreed to ship 86,100 tonnes of subsidised sugar to the Canary Islands, Madeira, Azores and the Aegean islands in 1997/98 (July/June), officials said.
The Canary islands will receive 60,000 tonnes, unchanged from this season.

But Madeira and the Azores were only initially granted half their annual quotas of 10,000 tonnes and 6,500 tonnes respectively pending the provision of more data by Portugal. Madeira's quota is unchanged but Azores' is 1,000 tonnes higher.
The Aegean islands quota was split into two with an inner ring allocated 600 tonnes, down from 3,000 tonnes this season. An outer ring of islands will receive an unchanged 9,000 tonnes.
